# LUMOS 3.1.3 Multi-Page Public Release

## v3.1.3 homepage branding

The Home hero now begins with a prominent LUMOS logo and wordmark, followed by a larger expanded system name. This strengthens immediate product recognition without changing the animated design statement, navigation, model workspaces, scientific contracts, or release architecture.

## Public presentation and navigation

- Removed release-number branding from the masthead, browser title, footer, installation metadata, and routine status messages.
- Added a dedicated Home page with product introduction, scientific positioning, domain entry points, lifecycle overview, guided tour, installation action, and documentation access.
- Replaced direct Markdown footer links and modal documentation with a permanent About & Methodology page.
- Expanded the footer and added Hudson Dong and LUMOS team attribution.
- Added an in-application About Us page, centralized scope guidance in Limitations, and preserved the complete scientific and operational model, reproducibility artifacts, collapsible layout, and map-focus mode.


LUMOS v3 is the first complete public release of the Localized Unified Monitoring Optimization System. It provides one static, browser-based system for environmental field reconstruction, monitoring design, cross-domain program allocation, verified deployment planning, field operations, commissioning, and maintenance across Heat, Air, Soil, and Water.

## Public capabilities

- Continuous probabilistic fields and uncertainty-aware monitoring placement.
- Social-information, fairness, reliability, budget, spacing, and feasibility constraints.
- Serious scientific baselines and reduced-instance exact benchmarks.
- Pre-intervention diagnosis and BACI-inspired post-intervention design.
- Domain-specific inference, transport, observations, validation, robustness, and evidence.
- Cross-domain initial budgets, sequential reallocation, adaptive multi-round simulation, and robust policy comparison.
- Coordinated host assignment, co-location savings, and correlated-failure reporting.
- Imported candidate inventories and explicit verified/conditional/unresolved/infeasible review states.
- Phased field campaigns, reserve sites, live outcome tracking, and adaptive replacement.
- Commissioning, procurement, permit, calibration, uptime, completeness, maintenance, tickets, and replacement planning.
- Browser-local workspaces, offline application-shell caching, and JSON/CSV evidence exports.
- Public architecture audit; internal release-quality checks remain repository tooling rather than a visitor-facing workspace.

## Professional release standards

The release is version consistent across application metadata, service worker, manifest, citation, documentation, and static build. Automated verification checks JavaScript syntax, credentials, scientific contracts, deterministic evidence, accessibility declarations, static asset size, and release completeness.

The interface includes a skip link, visible keyboard focus, reduced-motion support, a color-vision-safe palette, collapsible header and panels, and a Focus map control for a near-full-window map.

## Limitations and intended use

LUMOS is a planning and research system. A model estimate is not an observation; a mapped host is not permission; a reviewed record is not authenticated; a power estimate is not causal proof; a sampling plan is not a regulatory determination; a commissioning event is not a certified inspection; and a heuristic result is not globally optimal unless an exact reduced-instance result is explicitly labeled.

## Deployment

The public app remains fully static and compatible with GitHub Pages. Permanent credentials are prohibited from the frontend. Optional external sources degrade to systematic or frozen fallbacks where scientifically appropriate and must remain visibly labeled.

## Verification

```bash
npm run verify
```

See `docs/COMMISSIONING_AND_MAINTENANCE.md`, `docs/LIMITATIONS.md`, and `docs/PRIVACY_AND_DATA_GOVERNANCE.md` before operational use.


## Brand and Home refinement

The 3.1.3 public architecture uses separate static entry pages for Home, About Us, Documentation, Research & Process, Contact & Feedback, Unified, Heat, Air, Soil, and Water. A shared workspace shell and shared JavaScript model preserve one scientific implementation across every workspace URL, while lightweight informational pages keep public navigation clear. New sessions open at the full United States extent, while saved workspaces are restored only by explicit user action.


## v3.1.3 information architecture

The public site now separates About Us, Documentation, Research & Process, and Contact & Feedback into permanent pages. Research includes a manuscript and conference-status placeholder for the forthcoming LUMOS paper.
